claims.statement: EU electricity rules allow final customers to contract for aggregation without their supplier's consent and require access to relevant demand-response data.
Poland requires businesses providing aggregation to enter the URE aggregator register, which continues to list new entrants.
Demand hypothesis: aggregators will pay more for consented, meter-ready sites than for unqualified energy leads.

contrary_evidence: Aggregation itself is regulated in Poland, so careless contracting could cross the intended referral boundary.
Many small sites may not generate enough flexibility revenue to justify onboarding.

economics.acquisition_route: Demand hypothesis: the family installer and energy auditors can identify owners of controllable heat pumps, PV, batteries, and HVAC loads
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Hypothesis: 5000 active sites yielding 900 PLN annual platform revenue creates 4.5m PLN revenue; 25% EBITDA at a 5x data-network value could exceed 5m PLN in 5-7 years
economics.founder_time: 15-20 hours weekly; operate as a data and referral layer until regulated scope is confirmed
economics.gross_margin_basis: Economics hypothesis: 65-80% after site data validation, with hardware and aggregator operations excluded
economics.payback: Economics hypothesis: 100 accepted sites at 900 PLN plus modest recurring shares recover initial capital in 12-18 months
economics.pricing: Economics hypothesis: 500-1500 PLN per aggregator-accepted site plus 10-20% of onboarding or recurring gross revenue
economics.retention_or_repeat: Availability calendars, re-baselining, new devices, program switching, and recurring activations

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Site response history, baseline quality, owner permissions, and an increasingly valuable map of uncontracted flexible load
fingerprint.customer: Commercial properties, cold stores, warehouses, small industry, battery owners, and licensed aggregators
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Renewable installers, energy auditors, property managers, cold-chain vendors, and aggregator partnerships
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Owner mandate, device and meter inventory, baseline readiness, availability calendar, program matching, and handoff to registered aggregators
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Aggregator pays for an accepted qualified site and shares revenue after activation; owners can use the basic intake free
fingerprint.problem_trigger: An aggregator needs qualified flexible capacity, while an owner cannot compare programs or repeatedly package technical and authorization evidence

founder_fit: Algorithmic matching and baselining suit the founder

structure.commercial_archetype: Rights registry and regulated-market lead exchange
structure.control_point: Verified owner mandate plus meter-ready forward availability for each site
structure.critical_dependency: Licensed aggregators must accept the prequalification packet and provide transparent activation and revenue data

thesis: Commercial building and distributed-energy owners authorize a neutral prequalification layer to map controllable load, meter evidence, operating limits, and forward availability to licensed Polish aggregators. Demand hypothesis: scarce site readiness and clean owner mandates can be monetized without initially becoming the regulated aggregator.
title: Commercial Flexibility Rights Registry
